test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2024: Official Paper (Held On: 11 Jul, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In which year did a trio of scientists, Avery, MacLeod and McCarty, prove that except viruses, all living organisms have DNA as their genetic material?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1944**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In 1944, Oswald Avery, Colin MacLeod, and Maclyn McCarty conducted experiments that demonstrated that DNA is the substance that causes bacterial transformation.
 
• Their findings provided critical evidence that DNA is the hereditary material in organisms, excluding viruses, which can have RNA as their genetic material.
 
• This was one of the first significant steps in molecular biology that led to the identification of DNA as the carrier of genetic information.
 
• Their work built upon Frederick Griffith's experiment in 1928, which suggested the existence of a "transforming principle" that could transfer genetic information.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid)**

 
 
• DNA is a molecule that carries most of the genetic instructions used in the growth, development, functioning, and reproduction of all known living organisms and many viruses.
 
• DNA is composed of two strands that coil around each other to form a double helix, carrying the genetic instructions in sequences of four types of nucleotides: adenine (A), thymine (T), cytosine (C), and guanine (G).
 
 
 
• **RNA (Ribonucleic Acid)**
 
 
• RNA is a molecule essential in various biological roles in coding, decoding, regulation, and expression of genes.
 
• RNA is usually single-stranded and is composed of nucleotides: adenine (A), uracil (U), cytosine (C), and guanine (G).
 
• In some viruses, RNA acts as the genetic material instead of DNA.
 
 
 
• **Bacterial Transformation**
 
 
• Bacterial transformation is a process by which bacterial cells take up foreign DNA molecules and incorporate them into their own genetic material, leading to genetic changes.
 
• This process was first observed by Frederick Griffith in 1928, which led to the discovery of the "transforming principle" later identified as DNA by Avery, MacLeod, and McCarty.
 
 
 
• **Griffith's Experiment**
 
 
• Griffith's experiment demonstrated that a substance from dead bacteria could genetically transform living bacteria.
 
• He worked with two strains of Streptococcus pneumoniae: a virulent S strain with a smooth capsule and a non-virulent R strain without a capsule.
 
• His results showed that heat-killed S strain bacteria could transfer genetic material to the R strain, making it virulent.
